speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to help me understand your condition better, can you describe exactly what triggers these episodes and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The history of fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion eight weeks ago suggests a possible preceding viral infection. Since your symptoms worsen at night and with exertion, has anyone noticed if you wheeze or have a tight sensation in your chest during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Airway Dysfunction Syndrome (Post-viral cough variant asthma)
